note.question: How can service providers with private effort support contract design?
note.overview: We investigate the performance of two commonly used pricing schemes—hourly-rate contract and two-part tariff—in service environments where the buyer’s valuation is invisible to the service provider and the provider’s effort may not be visible to the buyer. In the private effort environment, we further distinguish between situations where the contract may be based on the outcome or on the effort reported by the provider. The paper shows that under the two-part tariff, when effort is private, the provider can achieve the same profit as under public effort by contracting on reported effort and will be worse off by contracting on outcome.

components.formal: Optimization rule: choose feasible decisions to optimize the stated objective.
conditions: In the canonical valuation scenario vL ≤vH, or ̃t ≤0, only candidate (a) is feasible, so the optimal solution still holds a simple structure, similar to the public effort environment.

Interestingly, the reduction of the provider’s ex- pected profit is through the buyer’s marginal value θx under a two-part tariff, as a result of the fixed slope of the optimal price line, while through his fixed value vx under hourly-rate contract, as a result of the fixed origin of the price line.

The optimal solution is more complicated in the noncanonical regimes under private effort because all three solution candidates may be interior solutions simultaneously (e.g., when (vL, vH) (2, 1), (θL, θH) (4, 5), λ 0.5, c 1, and δ 0.7).
By contrast, under public effort, at most one of the solution candidates, the true optimal one, can be an interior solution.
